blockingIssues.description: The fix hoists sdkSkills into a backend-agnostic shared map, so non-droid prompt-injection backends can inherit droid-only SDK skills and the new regression tests miss that negative case.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: When SDK-derived skill state is hoisted outside AcpSkillManager's enabledSkills cache key, require an explicit negative regression test proving non-droid prompt-injection backends do not inherit droid-only sdkSkills.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: m1-f1b added positive droid regression tests but no backend-isolation case; scrutiny found that a droid syncSdkSkills bootstrap can leak sdkSkills into the opencode/custom-workspace prompt-injection path.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: When mission guidance accepts a narrower evidence scope than the original validation contract, record that override in normative guidance and sync the validation contract before the next scrutiny re-run.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: m1-f4b passed under the accepted live-skill-inventory baseline, but validation-contract.md still encodes the older office-cli/reply-level expectations, creating avoidable validator drift.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Tighten the follow-procedure checklist so workers may only mark followedProcedure=true after invoking required startup skills in order and using desktop-app-testing for manual CDP verification.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: m1-f4b's final handoff claimed followedProcedure=true even though the transcript did not invoke desktop-app-testing and did not start with droid-sdk-integration as required by the skill.
